commit.message:
Fix phase name, add vm.flagless, use test.main.class

- Use "Iter GVN 1" instead of "After Iter GVN 1" (level 3 graph)
- Add vm.flagless requires since test spawns new VMs
- Use ${test.main.class} for @run directive
Use countOccurrences for accurate per-group phase count

Final review fixes

- Level 5: assert no Bytecode phase (level 6 only)
- Directive test: assert branchyMethod is NOT in output
- Multi-method: use assertEquals for exactly one Final Code
- Add braces to single-line if statement

Improve test per review feedback

- Remove PASSED printings
- Cache dumpAtLevel() results to avoid re-running JVMs
- Each level checks for level-specific phases AND asserts absence of
  phases from the next level (e.g., level 1 must NOT contain PhaseCCP 1)
- Level 1: add Before Matching check
- Level 4: add Initial Liveness check
- Level 6: check for per-bytecode graphs (Bytecode 0: ...)
- Remove redundant testLevelSpecificPhases() method
- Multi-method test: verify each method emits its own Final Code graph
  within its group
- IGVPrintLevel directive: use CompileCommand=IGVPrintLevel syntax,
  remove compileonly to test directive-only behavior

Extend IGV dump test coverage

- Cover all print levels (-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
- Check level-specific phases explicitly: Final Code at level 1+,
  PhaseCCP 1 only at level 2+, After Iter GVN Step only at level 5+
- Verify graph counts increase monotonically across levels
- Parse XML with javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilder to verify
  well-formedness (catches truncated/malformed output)
- Verify compiled method name appears in graph output
- Exercise multiple methods (compute + branchyMethod) and verify
  both appear as separate groups in the dump
- Test per-method IGVPrintLevel compiler directive with system
  level 0 to ensure directive-based dumping works independently

8370870: IGV: add simple regression tests for graph dumping

Add JTReg test that exercises IGV graph dumping at different
PrintIdealGraphLevel values and verifies the basic structure of
the generated XML files:

- Expected XML elements are present (graphDocument, group, graph,
  nodes, edges, controlFlow, method, bytecodes, properties)
- Higher print levels produce more phase dumps
- Output file is non-empty and well-formed
